messages.text:
Hello,
I’m considering your Hammer DC06:
https://heliumdeploy.com/products/hammer-miner-scrypt-dc06-330-mh-s
The listing is marked “Final Sale.” What exactly does that mean for returns, defective units, and warranty coverage?
Your photos appear to show a barrel power connector. I’ve seen DC06 units advertised elsewhere with an XT30 connection, including this listing:
https://dceminer.com/products/hammer-dc06-scrypt-miner-330-mh-s-asic-miner-for-ltc-doge-mining
Is the XT30 version a newer factory revision with changes to the power delivery system? Are your final-sale units older inventory being cleared out, or are they the latest hardware revision?
Before ordering, please confirm:

  *
Which board revision and power connector would I receive?
  *
Do you have the factory XT30 version available?
  *
Are the units new and unused?
  *
Are the matching power supply and stand included?
  *
What are the stock hashrate and actual power consumption at the wall?
  *
Where would it ship from, and what is the delivery time to (address hidden)?
  *
Are there any import charges or other fees beyond shipping and sales tax?
  *
Do you accept credit cards?

Please also send a photo of the actual hardware version currently shipping, showing the power connector and board revision.
Thank you.
Note to the team: I'll check our internal notes and the product details before answering.
Read the hammer miner scrypt dc06 330 mh s page
Read the hammer dc06 scrypt miner 330 mh s asic miner for ltc doge mining page

Hi Dean,

Thanks for the detailed list, and good to hear Harlo OS is treating you well.

On the hardware itself, here is what I can tell you with confidence. The D.06 we sell is the 330 MH/s Scrypt board rated at roughly 105 W, and it ships with a 12 V 10 A power supply in the box, with the AC plug matched to the shipping address. Wall draw will sit a little above the board figure once you count the supply's own conversion loss, so think low-to-mid 100s of watts on a meter rather than exactly 105. I will not quote you a measured wall number I have not seen on a meter myself. The 330 MH/s is the stock rating, and anything above that is a turbo or boost setting that runs hotter and voids the warranty.

On the connector question, I am not going to guess. The listing photos are our own, and I cannot confirm from here which board revision and which connector, barrel or XT30, is on the units sitting in the warehouse right now, or whether the XT30 version is a later factory revision with a different power delivery path. That is exactly the sort of thing our hardware lead JD checks against a unit in hand, so I have passed it to him along with your request for a photo of the hardware currently shipping, showing the connector and the board. The same note carries your other questions: what the Final Sale label means for returns, defective units and warranty, whether the stand is in the box, whether the units are new and unused, which warehouse a Colorado order ships from with its delivery time, any import or other charges, and the card question. A colleague is picking that up today and will come back to you on this thread.

Two things I can give you straight from our published terms, so you are not waiting on them. We accept Visa, Mastercard, American Express and Discover, plus crypto and Afterpay. On warranty, defective units are covered for return or exchange directly with us within 7 days of delivery, and after that the manufacturer warranty applies, a minimum of one year worldwide. How the Final Sale label interacts with that is the one point I want the team to confirm in writing rather than me paraphrasing it.

If you want a faster technical read in the meantime, our Discord is at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and JD is @nullhashrate there. He and the DC06 owners in that channel are very active, and someone will likely have both connector versions on a desk.

Hal, HeliumDeploy technical support

Hi Dean,

Thanks for your patience. Your questions are with the team, and the hardware side, the board revision, the connector and a photo of what is actually shipping, is with JD, our hardware lead. Someone is picking it up today and will reply on this thread.

While you wait, one thing worth knowing so the answer lands in context: on this class of board the connector choice is a wiring question rather than a performance one. A barrel jack and an XT30 both carry the same 12 V rail, the XT30 simply handles current with less contact resistance and will not pull out as easily. Whichever one you receive, the unit is rated at the same 330 MH/s on roughly 105 W, and the supply in the box is matched to the connector on that board, so there is nothing for you to source or adapt on your end.

If you want a quicker technical read in the meantime, the Discord is at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and JD is @nullhashrate there. Plenty of DC06 owners in that channel have both versions on a desk.

Hal, HeliumDeploy technical support

Thanks. I'll make a stop over there on the Discord.
My preference is the Xt30 connection. Not  a fan of the barrel connectors.

Again, thanks for the quick replay.

Dean

Hi Dean,

Noted, and that preference is now on the record with your other questions, so whoever comes back to you will answer specifically on whether an XT30 unit can be yours rather than just describing the two versions.

I understand the preference. On these desktop boards the barrel jack is the usual weak point over time, more from being knocked or tugged than from current, and an XT30 is a friction-locked pair that stays put. I cannot promise you one, because what is on the shelf is not something I can see from my side, so take that as the reason for your preference being sound rather than a commitment on which connector arrives.

Enjoy the Discord. JD is @nullhashrate and the DC06 owners there will tell you straight which revision they got and when.

Hal, HeliumDeploy technical support
